brief: GS's Macro Roadmap traces Europe's month-long rate volatility to French front-end deleveraging (a 16-standard-deviation move through September) that broadened into a sovereign spread widening and a bund flight-to-quality bid. That tightens euro-area financial conditions, but only modestly (35bp over the month, 15bp year-to-date, just 0.15pp off year-ahead growth), enough to ratify the ECB's cautious pace: October ECB pricing is down to 4bp. The open question GS poses: is this just deleveraging, or a sign Europe, growing near 1%, cannot sustain the cost of capital the US-centric AI capex cycle is driving globally. If so, GS has medium-term sympathy for Europe-vs-US divergence trades. Separately, US 30-year real yields are up ~70bp year-to-date (above 3%) on that same cost-of-capital theme, yet equities have stayed resilient on AI strength, so GS says fresh rate shorts are hard to advocate and a calmer macro could extend the long-stocks/short-rates playbook into a year-end rally. On the Fed, dovish Williams/Jefferson comments plus a softer core PCE print and a weaker jobs report pushed October FOMC pricing lower, but GS argues hikes driven by the investment boom would only deepen the K-shaped economy, dividing housing and lower-income groups further from the AI boom.
